chronicle.text: Daiyeim tied fiber and fiber together with fiber and was left with something to carry things in: the first carrier.
Kuyashek gathered food that had grown where seeds had been dropped: the first harvest from seed left in the ground.
Naizer drank from the sea and it did not quench their thirst.
Deido struck flint with flint and stared at what happened.
Deido struck flint with flint and was left with a sharp edge: the first blade.
Mairal tied a carrier and wood together with fiber and was left with something heavy on a handle: the first club.
Mairal went back to a thing they had made a third time, to see it happen again: the first deliberate testing.
Daiyeim scratched a mark <-..> into the ground.
Daiyeim buried seed on purpose, having seen it come back as food: the beginning of farming.
Retok struck flint where dry things lay, and they caught: the first fire made by people.
At (1, 17) the heap of things people had left grew big enough to keep out a fifth of the winter cold: the first dwelling. Yetu had put in the most.
Retok tied a bundle they had tied and a club together with fiber and was left with something that floats and carries someone across water: the first raft.
Retok came back for food left 5 weeks before, and it was still there.
Seirei took in the orphan Yeirubeis, no relation, the first time a stranger raised another's child.
Retok tied a club and fiber together with fiber and was left with something warm to wear: the first wrap.
5 people now take the mark <^..> to go with water, and have for two years. Nobody decided this; it grew from where the mark was made and seen.
Maimourai tied a blade and wood together with fiber and was left with a sharp point on a long shaft: the first spear.
Seivoyim found that what Ravoukair had told them was wrong, and trusted them less for it.
3 people now take the mark <o^^> to go with water, and have for two years. Nobody decided this; it grew from where the mark was made and seen.
Yetu set food aside on purpose, having found it there when it was needed before: the beginning of keeping stores.
8 people now take the mark <\-^> to go with water, and have for two years. Nobody decided this; it grew from where the mark was made and seen.
